plan.goal: Reproduce mid-range arterial wall shear stress of 15 dyn/cm² (1.5 Pa) on an endothelial-lined microfluidic channel.
plan.rationale:
Target shear is 1.5 Pa (15 dyn/cm²), the classic mid-range arterial wall shear value. This is deliberately above the HUVEC microvascular registry range (0.1–1 Pa) because the user explicitly requests an ARTERIAL model — arterial endothelium experiences ~1–2 Pa, and 1.5 Pa is the standard mid-arterial setpoint used in flow-adaptation studies.

Geometry: a wide rectangular channel 1000 µm (w) × 100 µm (h) × 20 mm (L). Using the wide-channel wall shear relation τ = 6·μ·Q/(w·h²) with μ = 1e-3 Pa·s (water-like medium), the flow rate needed for 1.5 Pa is Q = τ·w·h²/(6μ) = 150 µL/min. This is confirmed by the flow_rate_for_shear_stress and wall_shear_stress tools (150 µL/min → 1.5 Pa).

Flow checks: Reynolds ≈ 4.5 (firmly laminar, ≪2300), residence time ≈ 0.8 s/pass, pressure drop ≈ 600 Pa (~6 cm H₂O) — all well within syringe-pump capability. O₂ supply at 150 µL/min exceeds endothelial demand by ~800×, so no longitudinal hypoxia.

Seeding: HUVEC at 15,000 cells/cm² (mid of the 10–20k registry range) over the 2 cm² channel floor → 30,000 cells/channel. HUVEC doubling 24–72 h; a 2–3 day perfusion culture reaches confluence under flow.

Assumptions: medium viscosity ≈ 1e-3 Pa·s; wide-channel (w≫h) shear approximation valid at w/h = 10; single-pass flow (not recirculating) for the shear setpoint; HUVEC as the arterial endothelial surrogate.
caveats: Verify medium viscosity at 37 °C (assumed 1e-3 Pa·s; serum-supplemented medium can be slightly higher, which would raise shear at fixed Q).
The wide-channel shear formula assumes w≫h (here w/h=10); confirm with CFD or a full rectangular-channel correction if higher precision is needed.
HUVEC registry shear range is microvascular (0.1–1 Pa); 1.5 Pa is the arterial setpoint — confirm the specific HUVEC lot tolerates arterial shear (some lots show flow-adaptation time).
Confirm the syringe pump can deliver 150 µL/min steadily and that the ~600 Pa pressure drop is within the pump/tubing rating.
Prime the channel and check for bubbles before seeding; trapped air disrupts the monolayer and shear profile.
Coat the PDMS channel (e.g. fibronectin/collagen) for HUVEC adhesion before seeding.
Measure actual shear in situ (e.g. micro-PIV or bead tracking) rather than relying only on the analytical value.

plan.goal: Reproduce mid-range arterial wall shear stress (15 dyn/cm² = 1.5 Pa) on an endothelial monolayer in a perfused microfluidic channel.
plan.rationale: Arterial endothelium experiences wall shear in the ~1.5 Pa (15 dyn/cm²) range, higher than the microvascular range in the HUVEC registry entry. A wide, shallow channel (800 µm × 100 µm) is chosen to keep the flow laminar and the pressure drop modest while reaching 1.5 Pa. Using culture-medium viscosity ≈ 1e-3 Pa·s (water-like), flow_rate_for_shear_stress gives 120 µL/min for 1.5 Pa; wall_shear_stress confirms 1.5 Pa at that flow. Reynolds ≈ 4.4 (firmly laminar), pressure drop ≈ 600 Pa over 20 mm (well within syringe-pump capability), residence time ≈ 0.8 s/pass. HUVEC is the standard arterial-endothelium model; 1.5 Pa is above the registry microvascular range but is the physiologically correct arterial target.
caveats: 1.5 Pa (15 dyn/cm²) is arterial-range shear; the HUVEC registry physiological range is microvascular (sub-Pa) — confirm the arterial target is intended and that HUVEC tolerates it (monitor morphology/junctional markers).
Verify medium viscosity in the lab (≈1e-3 Pa·s assumed); serum and temperature shift it slightly.
Confirm the syringe pump can deliver 120 µL/min steadily; pressure drop ≈ 600 Pa over 20 mm is well within range.
Confirm the channel is fully wetted/degassed before flow to avoid air pockets that disrupt the monolayer.
Seed HUVEC at ~1.5e4 cells/cm² and allow confluence before applying flow; ramp flow up gradually to avoid shear-shock detachment.

plan.goal: Measure barrier integrity of a Caco-2 monolayer on a 1.12 cm² 12-well Transwell insert: report TEER, Papp, and clearance from resistance and flux measurements.
plan.rationale: Barrier integrity is assessed by two independent readouts. TEER is computed from the area-normalised resistance difference: (R_total − R_blank) × area = (900 − 150) Ω × 1.12 cm² = 840 Ω·cm². This sits within the mature Caco-2 range (250–1000 Ω·cm², model ~400–1200 Ω·cm²) and comfortably above the ~300 Ω·cm² QC gate, so the monolayer is suitable for a transport study. Papp is derived from the steady-state flux: (flux/60)/(area × donor conc) = (0.03/60)/(1.12 × 50) = 8.93e-6 cm/s. This is a leaky-monolayer-level Papp (tight barriers ≈ 1e-7–1e-6 cm/s), consistent with a paracellular probe crossing a Caco-2 monolayer. Clearance (permeability–surface-area product) = Papp × area = 8.93e-6 × 1.12 = 6.0e-4 mL/min. The flux cross-check (Papp × C₀ × area × 60 = 0.030 nmol/min) reproduces the measured 0.03 nmol/min, confirming internal consistency. Assumptions: medium viscosity/electrode geometry are standard for the 12-well insert; blank resistance is measured on a cell-free coated insert in the same medium; steady-state flux is reached before sampling.
caveats: Confirm the blank (150 Ω) is measured on a cell-free insert with the same coating and medium, at the same temperature, to avoid a systematic TEER offset.
Verify steady-state flux was actually reached (multiple time points with linear cumulative transport) before quoting Papp; a single-point flux can bias the value.
TEER 840 Ω·cm² is within range but Papp 8.9e-6 cm/s is at the leaky end — confirm the probe is a true paracellular marker (e.g. Lucifer yellow / FITC-dextran) and not actively transported.
Check the electrode is calibrated and the reading is in Ω (not kΩ) before applying the area factor.
Report TEER as area-normalised Ω·cm², never a bare ohm reading.

plan.goal: Determine how many 96-well plate wells can be plated from a counted primary human hepatocyte suspension at standard sandwich-culture density.
plan.rationale: Hemocytometer count: 40 cells/square × 2 (dilution) × 10^4 = 800,000 cells/mL. Total cells from 0.36 mL = 288,000. Primary human hepatocytes (sandwich culture) plate at 100,000–200,000 cells/cm² (registry range). A 96-well has ~0.32 cm² growth area, giving 32,000 cells/well at the low end and 64,000 cells/well at the high end. 288,000 ÷ 32,000 = 9 wells; 288,000 ÷ 64,000 = 4 wells. Primary hepatocytes do not divide in vitro, so the plated count is the final count — no growth correction applies.

The 4–9 well range depends on the plating density chosen within the 100,000–200,000 cells/cm² sandwich-culture range; pick one density and state it explicitly.

plan.goal: Culture human proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTECs) in a perfused microchannel that reproduces the in vivo apical fluid shear of ~0.2 dyn/cm² (0.02 Pa).
plan.rationale: Human proximal tubular epithelial cells experience a low apical fluid shear in vivo, commonly cited around 0.2 dyn/cm² (0.02 Pa). The physiology registry has no PTEC profile, so this target is taken from the kidney-tubule literature (proximal tubule luminal shear is low, ~0.1-0.5 dyn/cm², far below vascular endothelium). A wide, shallow channel (1000 µm × 100 µm) is chosen so that the wall shear formula τ = 6·μ·Q/(w·h²) applies (wide-channel approximation, w >> h). At 2 µL/min with water-like medium (μ = 1e-3 Pa·s), τ = 6·1e-3·(2/1e6/60)/(1000e-6·(100e-6)²) = 0.02 Pa = 0.2 dyn/cm², matching the target. Reynolds number is 0.06 (deeply laminar), residence time over the 20 mm channel is ~60 s, and the pressure drop is only ~8 Pa, well within syringe-pump capability. PTECs are seeded at ~8e4 cells/cm² (typical renal epithelial seeding density) onto the 0.2 cm² channel floor = 16,000 cells. Medium viscosity is assumed water-like (1e-3 Pa·s).
caveats: The physiology registry has no PTEC profile — the 0.2 dyn/cm² target is from the kidney-tubule literature and should be verified against the specific primary/immortalized PTEC source (e.g. RPTEC, HK-2) being used.
Confirm the wide-channel shear approximation (w >> h) holds for the actual device; if the channel is narrower or has rounded corners, the 6·μ·Q/(w·h²) formula overestimates shear.
Verify medium viscosity (≈1e-3 Pa·s assumed); serum or additives can raise it slightly.
Confirm the pump can deliver a stable 2 µL/min (low-flow syringe pumps or pressure-driven flow may be needed).
Check PTEC attachment and monolayer formation under flow; seed at high density and allow static adhesion before starting perfusion.
Validate that 0.2 dyn/cm² is the intended in vivo reference for the specific nephron segment — proximal tubule shear can vary with segment and species.

plan.rationale: The in vivo apical shear on human proximal tubular epithelial cells is approximately two-tenths of a dyne per square centimetre, which equals twenty millipascals. plan.goal: Design a venular microfluidic channel that recapitulates physiological venular wall shear stress (~0.15 Pa) on a perfused HUVEC endothelium.
plan.rationale:
Venular wall shear stress is on the low end of the microvascular range, typically ~0.1–0.5 Pa. HUVEC (the standard endothelial line for vascular OOC) has a physiological shear range of 0.1–1 Pa (registry), so a target of 0.15 Pa is both physiologically representative of venules and within the HUVEC tolerance window.

Geometry: an 800 µm × 100 µm × 20 mm rectangular channel (typical OOC dimensions; 0.16 cm² culture area). Using the wide-channel wall shear relation τ = 6·μ·Q/(w·h²) with μ = 1e-3 Pa·s (water-like medium), a flow of 12 µL/min gives τ = 0.15 Pa. This is confirmed by the inverse calculation (flow_rate_for_shear_stress → 12 µL/min).

Flow regime checks: Reynolds ≈ 0.44 (firmly laminar, ≪2300), residence time ≈ 8 s across the channel, pressure drop ≈ 60 Pa (trivially supplied by a syringe pump). O₂ supply/demand ratio ≈ 833 (no hypoxia; endothelial OCR ~0.02 fmol/s/cell assumed since HUVEC has no registry OCR).

Seeding: HUVEC at 15,000 cells/cm² (mid-range of the 10,000–20,000 registry range) over 0.16 cm² → ~2,400 cells/channel. Cells are seeded statically and allowed to attach/confluent before flow is ramped up to 12 µL/min.

Assumptions: medium viscosity ≈ water (1e-3 Pa·s); venular shear target 0.15 Pa chosen as representative of the venular low-shear regime; HUVEC OCR estimated at 0.02 fmol/s/cell (not in registry).
caveats: Verify the actual venular shear target against your specific literature source — venular shear is reported ~0.1–0.5 Pa; 0.15 Pa is a representative low-shear value.
Confirm medium viscosity at 37 °C (assumed 1e-3 Pa·s, water-like); serum-supplemented medium can be slightly higher.
Ramp flow up gradually (e.g. 2→6→12 µL/min over 24–48 h) after static seeding to avoid acute shear-induced detachment; HUVEC needs time to form a confluent monolayer before full flow.
Confirm HUVEC attachment/coating (e.g. fibronectin/collagen) for the PDMS channel surface.
HUVEC OCR is not in the registry — the O₂ supply check used an assumed 0.02 fmol/s/cell; verify if you plan high-density or long-term culture.
Check the syringe pump can deliver 12 µL/min stably and that the 60 Pa pressure drop is within the pump/tubing rating.
Validate endothelial health by morphology and junctional markers (VE-cadherin), not TEER, since HUVEC barrier is low (~20–100 Ω·cm²).

plan.goal: Recapitulate physiological venular wall shear stress (~0.5 Pa) on a HUVEC-lined microfluidic channel.
plan.rationale: Venular endothelium experiences low shear, at the lower end of the HUVEC physiological range from the cell_physiology registry. I chose a standard OOC channel (400 µm wide x 100 µm high x 20 mm long) and solved for the flow rate that gives 0.5 Pa wall shear stress with culture-medium viscosity (1e-3 Pa·s): 20 µL/min. This is verified by the calculators: wall_shear_stress(20,400,100,1e-3) = 0.5 Pa; Reynolds = 1.33 (firmly laminar, well below 2300); residence time = 2.4 s; pressure drop = 200 Pa (~2 cm H2O, easily supplied by a syringe pump). HUVEC seeded at 15,000 cells/cm2 (within the registry range) on the 0.08 cm2 channel floor gives 1,200 cells. The 0.5 Pa target sits mid-venular and is well within the HUVEC viability window.
caveats: Verify HUVEC monolayer confluence and junctional morphology (VE-cadherin) before perfusion; HUVEC TEER is low and not a reliable barrier readout.
Confirm medium viscosity in-house; the 0.5 Pa shear assumes 1e-3 Pa·s.
Prime the channel and degas PDMS to avoid air bubbles that disrupt the monolayer under flow.
Confirm the syringe pump delivers 20 µL/min accurately at this low rate; use a glass syringe and appropriate tubing.
Venular shear is a range; 0.5 Pa is the upper venular value — if a lower venular shear is desired, reduce flow proportionally.

plan.goal: Scale a body-on-chip skin compartment to a 70 kg adult (cardiac output 5000 mL/min) carrying 5e6 cells, reporting the skin organ flow fraction and the organ flow rate it receives.
plan.rationale: Skin receives ~5% of resting cardiac output in a thermoneutral adult (literature range 5-10%, rising with heat stress). With cardiac output = 5000 mL/min, the skin organ flow rate = 0.05 × 5000 = 250 mL/min. The chip carries 5e6 cells; adult human skin contains roughly 10^11 cells (≈1.8 m², ~5×10^10-10^11 cells), giving an allometric scale of ~5e-5. The chip's share of organ flow = 250 mL/min × 5e-5 ≈ 0.0125 mL/min ≈ 12.5 µL/min. Skin is not in the physiology registry, so these are standard textbook physiological anchors and must be verified against the specific literature used.
caveats: Skin organ flow fraction is thermoregulation-dependent (5-10% of cardiac output); the 5% figure assumes resting, thermoneutral conditions — verify against the specific reference used.
The allometric scale factor depends on the assumed total cell count of adult human skin (~10^11 cells); if a different skin cell mass is assumed, the chip flow scales proportionally.
Skin is not in the physiology registry — physiological targets are unverified and should be confirmed against primary literature.
The chip flow of ~12.5 µL/min is a scaling estimate; confirm the pump can deliver it stably and that the resulting wall shear stress is within the skin microvascular range.

plan.goal: Extrude bioink through a 150 µm nozzle along a 20733 µm path at 46.53 mm/min and report fill lines, deposition rate, and extruded volume.
plan.rationale: Fill lines = ceil(footprint_width / line_pitch) = ceil(33133/202) = 165. Extruded volume over the straight path = π(d/2)²·L = π(75 µm)²·20733 µm = 366.38 nL. Print time = L/v = 20733 µm / (46.53 mm/min) = 26.74 s. Deposition rate = volume/time = 366.38 nL / 0.4456 min ≈ 822 nL/min. Mean velocity u = Q/(w·h) = 0.466 mm/s; channel volume V = w·h·L = 1.287 µL; residence time τ = V/Q = 45.7 s; pressure drop dP = 12·μ·Q·L/(w·h³) = 33.1 Pa; wall shear τ_w = 6·μ·Q/(w·h²) = 0.0552 Pa. Reynolds number ≈ 0.044 confirms laminar flow. The wall shear (0.055 Pa ≈ 0.55 dyn/cm²) falls at the low end of the hepatic sinusoidal range (0.05–0.15 Pa), appropriate for a liver-sinusoid model. Assumptions: Newtonian fluid, fully developed laminar flow, wide-channel approximation for shear (w ≫ h), medium density 1000 kg/m³.
caveats: Verify the wide-channel approximation holds: w/h = 12, so the 6·μ·Q/(w·h²) shear formula is a good approximation but not exact; a full aspect-ratio correction would give a slightly higher wall shear.
Confirm the actual medium viscosity at 37 °C — 0.0014 Pa·s is higher than water-like medium (~0.001 Pa·s) and should be measured if the shear target is critical.
Check that the syringe pump delivers the stated 1.69 µL/min accurately at this low flow rate (pump pulsation/backlash can dominate).
Confirm PDMS channel dimensions by profilometry/measurement, as molded channels deviate from design values.
